steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Every statistical investigation has constraints that limit what is possible.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Time constraints affect how long you can spend collecting and analysing data.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cost constraints limit the resources available — equipment, travel, printing, software.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethical issues include obtaining consent, avoiding harm, and being honest about results.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name three practical constraints that might affect a statistical investigation. | Q: Why is confidentiality important in a statistical investigation? | Q: How can a pilot study help with investigation design?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Time, cost, and access to participants or equipment. | To protect participants' privacy and comply with data protection laws; it also encourages honest responses. | It identifies practical problems, unclear questions and constraints before the main data collection begins.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When asked about constraints, be specific — give concrete examples relevant to the investigation. Ethics questions often ask about consent and confidentiality — mention both. Use the term 'pilot study' when discussing how to test an investigation design. If evaluating an investigation, always comment on constraints and how they affect conclusions. Remember that constraints are not just negatives — they shape good investigation design.
